summary: Adds a Flask search endpoint and a hardcoded payment key, changes item pagination, downgrades lodash, and loosens the Dockerfile, CI workflow and deploy script.

findings.title: Search query built from request input
findings.description: search_items puts the q request parameter straight into the SQL text with an f-string. A quote in q ends the string literal and lets the caller add their own SQL. Any caller of /search can read every table in items.db. An attacker can also change rows or skip the filter. Pass q to cur.execute as a bound parameter with a placeholder.
findings.suggested_change: cur.execute("SELECT id, name, price FROM items WHERE name = ?", (q,))
findings.problem: search_items puts the q request parameter straight into the SQL text with an f-string. A quote in q ends the string literal and lets the caller add their own SQL.
findings.consequence: Any caller of /search can read every table in items.db. An attacker can also change rows or skip the filter.
findings.fix: Pass q to cur.execute as a bound parameter with a placeholder.

findings.title: Payment API key committed in source
findings.description: config.py stores a live-format Stripe secret key as a string literal. Anyone with access to the repository can read the key. Anyone holding the key can make charges and refunds and read customer payment data on the shop account. Revoke the key in Stripe and load the replacement from an environment variable or a secret store.
findings.problem: config.py stores a live-format Stripe secret key as a string literal. Anyone with access to the repository can read the key.
findings.consequence: Anyone holding the key can make charges and refunds and read customer payment data on the shop account.
findings.fix: Revoke the key in Stripe and load the replacement from an environment variable or a secret store.

findings.title: Pagination offset skips the first page
findings.description: list_items now computes offset as page times PAGE_SIZE. Page 1, the default, therefore starts at row 20 instead of row 0. Clients never see the first 20 items. Every later page is shifted by one page. Restore the offset to page minus one, times PAGE_SIZE.

findings.consequence: Clients never see the first 20 items. Every later page is shifted by one page.
findings.fix: Restore the offset to page minus one, times PAGE_SIZE.

findings.title: Pull request title interpolated into shell
findings.description: The new step pastes the pull request title into the run script before the shell parses it. A title containing a quote or command substitution runs as shell code. Any pull request author can run commands on the CI runner. They can also read its token and secrets. Pass the title through an env entry and reference it as a quoted shell variable.

findings.consequence: Any pull request author can run commands on the CI runner. They can also read its token and secrets.
findings.fix: Pass the title through an env entry and reference it as a quoted shell variable.

findings.title: Lodash downgraded to a vulnerable release
findings.description: The change pins lodash back from 4.18.1 to 4.17.15. Version 4.17.15 has known command injection, prototype pollution and ReDoS flaws. Front-end code that uses template, zipObjectDeep, unset or trim on untrusted input becomes exploitable. Keep lodash at 4.18.1 or later in package.json and package-lock.json.

findings.consequence: Front-end code that uses template, zipObjectDeep, unset or trim on untrusted input becomes exploitable.
findings.fix: Keep lodash at 4.18.1 or later in package.json and package-lock.json.

findings.title: Container now runs as root
findings.description: The change removed the USER 10001 line and the useradd step. The Flask server now runs as root inside the container. A flaw such as the search injection gets root inside the container. That makes container escape and tampering easier. Restore the unprivileged app user and the USER 10001 instruction before CMD.

findings.consequence: A flaw such as the search injection gets root inside the container. That makes container escape and tampering easier.
findings.fix: Restore the unprivileged app user and the USER 10001 instruction before CMD.

findings.title: Unguarded recursive delete of deploy directory
findings.description: The change removed the empty-value guard and the quotes from the rm target. With DEPLOY_DIR set to an empty string, the script deletes the root directory recursively. A misconfigured deploy can wipe the host filesystem. A path with spaces also deletes the wrong directories. Restore the quoted, guarded expansion.

findings.consequence: A misconfigured deploy can wipe the host filesystem. A path with spaces also deletes the wrong directories.

findings.title: Deploy loop parses ls output
findings.description: The loop now splits unquoted ls output on whitespace. It also prints bare names instead of the full paths the glob gave. Names with spaces are reported as several files, so the deploy log is wrong. Restore the quoted glob loop.

findings.consequence: Names with spaces are reported as several files, so the deploy log is wrong.

findings.title: Base image tag unpinned
findings.description: The change replaced the pinned python 3.12.7 slim image with python:latest. The latest tag moves to new Python major and minor releases without notice. Builds stop being reproducible. A Python upgrade can break the app silently, and the full image is much larger. Restore the pinned slim tag.

findings.consequence: Builds stop being reproducible. A Python upgrade can break the app silently, and the full image is much larger.

findings.title: Non-interactive apt install without -y
findings.description: The apt-get install call has no -y flag. If apt must pull in or upgrade extra packages, it asks for confirmation and gets no answer. The image build aborts whenever apt needs a confirmation. Add -y and --no-install-recommends, and clean the apt lists in the same layer.
findings.suggested_change: RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends curl && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
findings.problem: The apt-get install call has no -y flag. If apt must pull in or upgrade extra packages, it asks for confirmation and gets no answer.
findings.consequence: The image build aborts whenever apt needs a confirmation.
findings.fix: Add -y and --no-install-recommends, and clean the apt lists in the same layer.

findings.title: Changed endpoints have no tests
findings.description: The repository has no tests for the new search_items endpoint. Nothing tests the changed list_items offset either. Both the injection and the pagination regression reached review undetected. Add tests that hit /search with a quote in q and check /items page 1 starts at the first row.
findings.problem: The repository has no tests for the new search_items endpoint. Nothing tests the changed list_items offset either.
findings.consequence: Both the injection and the pagination regression reached review undetected.
findings.fix: Add tests that hit /search with a quote in q and check /items page 1 starts at the first row.

In order to execute raw query safely, prepared statement should be used. SQLAlchemy provides TextualSQL to easily used prepared statement with named parameters. For complex SQL composition, use SQL Expression Language or Schema Definition Language. In most cases, SQLAlchemy ORM will be a better option.

Alternatively, consider using the Django object-relational mappers (ORM) instead of raw SQL queries.
